paras: Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once passed by a person who was making du'aa saying, "O Allaah! Grant me patience." Rasulullaah ﷺ addressed the man saying, "You have asked Allaah for difficulty, now ask him for safety." Rasulullaah ﷺ then passed by another Mu'mineen who was making du'aa saying, "O Allaah! I ask you for the perfect bounty." "O son of Aadam Rasulullaah ﷺ asked, "Do you know what the perfect bounty is?" The man's response was, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ I only made the du'aa hoping for the best." Rasulullaah ﷺ explained, "The perfect bounty is to gain entry into Jannah and to be rescued from Jahannam." Thereafter he passed by yet another person making du'aa, saying, "O Dhul Jalaali wal Ikraam!" Addressing this person, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Your du'aa as been accepted, so ask (what you need)."
sources: Ibn Abi Shaybah, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal ' (Vol.1 Pg.292).

paras: Hadhrat Anas bin Maalik (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once went to visit a man who was suffering so much that he (had lost a lot of weight and) looked like a defeathered fledgling. "Is there any particular du'aa that you have been making to Allaah?" Rasulullaah ﷺ asked the man. The man informed Rasulullaah ﷺ that the du'aa he always made was, "O Allaah! Please bring forward to this world whatever punishment is due to me in the Aakhkah." Rasulullaah ﷺ told him, "Why do you rather not say: "O our Rabb, grant us (all that which is) good in this world, (all that which is) good in the Aakhirah and save us from the punishment of the fire (ofjahannam)." (Surah Baqarah, verse 201) The man then made the du'aa and was cured.
sources: Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Najjaar, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal '(Vol.1 Pg.290).

paras: Hadhrat Basheer bin Khasaasiyah (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once said to him, "Trunk Allaah for bringing you from the Rabee'ah Khath'am tribe and allowing you to accept Islaam at the hands of His Rasool ﷺ "O Rasulullaah Hadhrat Basheer (RA) said, "Pray to Allaah to allow me to die before you." Refusing the request, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "I shall not make that du'aa for anyone."'

Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b (RA) says, "Whenever making du'aa for anyone, Rasulullaah ﷺ always began with (asking for) himself. When speaking of Hadhrat Moosa (RA) one day, Rasulullaah ﷺ remarked, 'May Allaah shower His mercy on Moosa. Had he been more patient, he would have seen even stranger things from his companion. However, he said: "If I question you about anything after this, then you need not remain with me. You have received (enough) excuse from me (to part from me)." (Surah Kahaf, verse 72)
sources: Abu Nu'aym, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg.147).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Ayyoob Ansaari (RA) also reports that whenever Rasulullaah ﷺ made du'aa, he began with himself. ' '

Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) once said to Ibn Abu Saa'ib who was the lecturer of Madinah, "Refrain from going out of your way to rhyme your du'aa because 1 have seen the timcof Rasulullaah ﷺ and the Sahabah (RA) and none of them did this."
sources: Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad,, Abu Dawood, Nasa'ee and others, as Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.1 Pg.290). Tirmidhi has reported a similar narration, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.1 Pg.290).

paras: When Hadhrat Umar (RA) overheard a man making du'aa to be protected from tests, he remarked, "O Allaah! I seek Your protection from his words." He then addressed the man saying, "Are you asking your Rabb not to grant you a family and wealth?" Another narration states that Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "Do you want your Rabb not to grant you wealth and children? Whoever seeks protection from tests should seek protection from tests that lead people astray." ''* Hadhrat Muhaarib bin Dithaar narrates that his uncle said, "I used to pass by the house of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) just before dawn and would hear him make du'aa saying, 'O Allaah! You have called me and I have come. You have given me a command and I have obeyed. This is now the time before dawn, so do forgive me.' When I met Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA), I told him about this du'aa that I heard him say. He said, Verily Hadhrat Ya'qoob (RA) postponed making du'aa for his sons until the time of pre dawn.
sources: Shaybah and Abu Ubayd, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal ' (Vol.1 Pg.289).

paras: Hadhrat Umar (RA) says, "Whenever he made du'aa, Rasulullaah ﷺ raised his hands and after completing, he would pass them over his face."
sources: Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.10 Pg.155) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Another narration states that when raising his hands to make du'aa, Rasulullaah SPS-? would not drop them until he passed them over his face (upon completing the du'aa).
sources: Haakim.

paras: Hadhrat Umar (RA) also said, "I saw Rasulullaah ﷺ making du'aa at Ahjaaruz Zayt with his palms (towards his face) and when he completed, he passed them over his face."
sources: Tirmidhi.

paras: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ used to raise his hands for so long when making du'aa that I would get tired."
sources: Abdul Ghani in his Idaahul Ashkaal, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.1 Pg.289).

paras: Another narration adds that Rasulullaah ﷺ made du'aa saying, "O Allaah! I am but a human. Please do not punish me for verbally abusing or hurting anyone." Yet another narration reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "O Allaah! I am but a human so please do not punish me. If I have hurt any Mu'min or verbally abused him, then please do not punish me for it."
sources: Ahmad, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.10 Pg.168).
Abdur Razzaaq, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.1 Pg.291).

paras: Hadhrat Urwa (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once passed by a tribe of Bedouins who had accepted Islaam and whose settlement the coalition of Kuffaar armies had destroyed. Raising his hands and extending them before his face, Rasulullaah ﷺ cursed the coalition. "May my parents be sacrificed for you, O Rasulullaah ﷺ one of the Bedouins said, "Extend your hands even further." Rasulullaah ﷺ then extended his hands further from his face without raising them higher towards the sky. ' Abu Nu'aym Wahab reports that he saw both Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) and Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr (RA) pass their hands over their faces after making du'aa.
sources: Abdur Razzaaq, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.1 Pg.291)..
Bukhaari in his Adab (Pg.90).

paras: Hadhrat Qais Madani narrates that when a man came to ask Hadhrat Zaid bin Thaabit something, he said to the man, "Go to Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah because it once happened that Abu Hurayrah someone else and I were in the Masjid engaging in Dhikr and making du'aa when Rasulullaah ﷺ came to sit with us. When we fell silent, Rasulullaah ﷺ asked us to continue doing what we had been doing. My companion and I then started making du'aa before Abu Hurayrah and Rasulullaah ﷺ said 'Aameen' to our du'aas. Abu Hurayrah then started making du'aa and said, 'O Allaah! 1 ask You for everything that my two companions have asked for as well as knowledge that I shall never forget.' When Rasulullaah ﷺ said and I sad, 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ We also ask for knowledge that we shall never forget.' Rasulullaah ﷺ said, 'The man of the Daus tribe (Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA)) has beaten you to it.
sources: Tabraani in his Awsat, as quoted in Majma'uz Zawaa'id (Vol.9 Pg.321).

paras: Hadhrat Jaami bin Shaddaad narrates from a relative that he once heard Hadhrat Umar say, "I want you people to say 'Aameen' to three du'aas that I am going to make." He then proceeded to make du'aa saying, "O Allaah! I am weak so please strengthen me. O Allaah! I am stern, so please soften me. O Allaah! I am miserly so please make me generous."
sources: Ibn Sa'd (Vol.3 Pg.275)

paras: Hadhrat Saa'ib bin Yazeed reports that it was early one morning during the Year of Ashes (the year, in which Madinah experienced a crippling drought) that he saw Hadhrat Umar (RA) humbling himself before Allaah, wearing simple clothing and a shawl that barely reached his knees. He was seeking Allaah's forgiveness in a loud voice as his tears flowed on to his cheeks. (Rasulullaah ﷺ's uncle) Hadhrat Abbaas bin Abdul Muttalib (RA) was standing on his right side as he faced the Qibla and raised his hands as he sobbed before his Rabb. The people also made du'aa as he made du'aa, after which he took Hadhrat Abbaas (RA)'s hand and said, "O Allaah! Do accept the intercession of Rasulullaah ﷺ's uncle on our behalf." Hadhrat Abaas (RA) then stood beside Hadhrat Umar for a very long time, his eyes flowing with tears as he made du'aa to Allaah.
sources: IbnSa'd (Vol.3Pg.321).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed who was the freed slave of Hadhrat Usayd reports, "Hadhrat Umar used to patrol the Masjid at night and remove from there everyone besides the person engaged in salaah. When he once passed by a group of Sahabah (RA) amongst whom was Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b (RA), he asked, 'Who are you men?1 Hadhrat Ubay (RA) replied, 'We are members of your family, O Ameerul Mu'mineen.' 'What kept you behind after the salaah?' Hadhrat Umar asked. When they informed him that they had been engaged in Dhikr, Hadhrat Umar (RA) sat with them. He then said to the person closest to him, 'Take (the lead in making du'aa).' The man started making du'aa and (when he had completed) Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked each person to make du'aa until he came to me, who was sitting next to him. 'Come on,' he said to me. 1 was tongue-tied and started to shiver so much until he could actually feel me shake. He then said, '(Say something) Even if you have to only say, 'O Allaah forgive me. O Allaah! Have mercy on me.' Hadhrat Umar (RA) then started making du'aa and there was none who wept more than him. Thereafter, he said, 'That is enough. You may all disperse.
sources: IbnSa'd(Vol.3Pg.294).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Habeeb bin Maslamah Fahri was a person whose du'aas were always accepted. When he was once appointed commander of an army and after making the necessary preparations, he was facing the Roman army when he said to the others, "I have heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, "When a group assembles and they all say 'Aameen' as one of them makes du'aa, Allaah certainly acts the du'aa.'" He then duly praised Allaah and said, "O Allaah! Protect our blood and still grant us the reward of martyrs." He was still making du'aa when the commander of the Roman army entered Hadhrat Habeeb (RA)'s tent (to surrender). In the chapter discussing the yearning that the Sahabah (RA) had for martyrdom and the du'aas they made for, in it the narration has already passed in which Hadhrat Nu'maan bin Muqarrin (RA) said, "I am to make a du'aa to Allaah which I stress that every person say 'Aameen' to. (He then made the du'aa saying) O Allaah! Grant Nu'maan martyrdom today with your assistance to the Muslims and make them victorious." Another narration adds that the others then said 'Aameen' to the du'aa.
sources: Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.10 Pg.170) has commented on the chain of narrators.
Tabari, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol. 6 Pg.216). Haakim (Vol.3 Pg.293) has reported a similar narration.

paras: Hadhrat Uqba bin Aamir (RA) states, "It was with regard to a person called Abdullaah Dhul Bijaadayn that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, 'Indeed, he is one who sighs very deeply.' This Rasulullaah ﷺ said because Abdullaah Dhul Bijaadayn used to engage in Dhikr abundantly by reciting the Qur'aan and making du'aa and all this he did in an audible voice." Requesting Du'aas from the Pious.
sources: Ahmad and Tabraani, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.369). Ibn Jareer has reported a similar narration, as quoted in the Tafseeroi Ibn Katheer (Vol.2 Pg.395).

paras: Hadhrat Umar (RA) narrates that when he once requested Rasulullaah ﷺ for permission to perform Umrah, Rasulullaah ﷺ granted him permission and said, "Dear brother! Do not forget us in your du'aas." Hadhrat Umar (RA) says, "Those words gave me more joy than even the entire world could not."
sources: Abu Dawood and Tirmidhi. Ibn Sa'd (Vol.3 Pg.273) has reported a similar narration.

paras: Hadhrat Abu Umaama Baahili (RA) says, "When Rasulullaah ﷺ came to us once, we wished that he would make du'aa for us. He then said, 'O Allaah forgive us, have mercy on us, be pleased with us, accept from us, enter us into Jannah, save us from Jahannam and mend all our affairs." When we wished that he would make more du'aa, he said, "I have already included all your affairs (in the du'aa)."
sources: Ibn Abi Shaybah, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.1 Pg.29I).

paras: Hadhrat Talha bin Ubaydullaah (RA) narrates that a Sahabi once removed his excess clothing and then started to roll in the hot sand, saying to himself, "Taste the fire of Jahannam. You lie like a corpse in the night (without engaging in Ibaadah) and waste time during the day!" As he was doing this, he happened to see Rasulullaah ﷺ under the shade of a tree. He then approached Rasulullaah ﷺ and excused himself saying, "My Nafs got the better of me." "In fact," Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "the doors of the heavens have all been thrown open for you and the angels are boasting about you." Rasulullaah ﷺ then addressed the other Sahabah (RA) saying, "Take your journey's provisions from your brother (ask him for du'aas)." When one of the Sahabah (RA) asked the Sahabi to make du'aa for him, Rasulullaah ﷺ added, "Include them all (in your du'aa)." The Sahabi prayed, "O Allaah! Make Taqwa their journey's provision and guide them in all their affairs." "O Allaah!" Rasulullaah ﷺ said in between, "Guide him (to continue making du'aa)." The Sahabi then concluded by saying, "O Allaah! Make Jannah their final destination." ''* Hadhrat Buraydah Si! reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ was travelling somewhere when he came across a Sahabi rolling from his back to his belly in the hot sand as he chided himself saying, "O Nafs! You hope for Jannah when you sleep at night and waste your time during the day!" When he had regained his composure, he approached the Sahabah (RA). Rasulullaah ﷺ then instructed the Sahabah (RA) to request him for du'aas and when they did, the Sahabi prayed, "O Allaah! Guide them in all their affairs." "Pray some more," the Sahabah (RA) requested. He then said, "O Allaah! Make Taqwa their journey's provisions." The Sahabah (RA) again asked for more du'aas. This time, Rasulullaah ﷺ also asked him to make more du'aa for them and prayed to Allaah to inspire him. The Sahabi then said, "O Allaah! Make Jannah their final destination."
sources: Ibn Abi Dunya, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.1 Pg.290).

paras: Hadhrat Aseer bin Jaabir narrates that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) requested Hadhrat Uwais Qarni to seek forgiveness on his behalf, Hadhrat Uwais asked, "How can I seek forgiveness on your behalf when you are a companion of Rasulullaah ﷺ ?" Hadhrat Umar (RA) replied, " I have heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, Verily the best of all the Taabi'een (Muslims who have met the Sahabah shall be a man called Uwais."
sources: Tabraani. Haythami (Vol. 10 Pg. 185) has commented on the chain of narrators. Abu Nu'aym has reported a similar narration, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol .1 Pg.308).

paras: Another narration states that Rasulullaah ﷺ also added, "Whoever meets him (Hadhrat Uwais), must request him to seek forgiveness on your behalf."
sources: Ibnsa'd (Vol.6 Pg. 163).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Roomi narrates that Hadhrat Anas bin Maalik (RA) was in Zaawiya (close to Basrah) when someone said to him, "Some of your brothers from Basrah have come to you so that you may make du'aa for them." Hadhrat Anas immediately made du'aa saying, "O Allaah! Forgive us and shower Your mercy on us. Grant us the best of this world, the best of the Aakhirah and save us from Jahannam." When they requested for more du'aa, Hadhrat Anas repeated the du'aa and then said, "If you have been granted this, you have been granted the best of this world and the Aakhirah."

Hadhrat Yazeed bin Asam reports that a man from Shaam was a fierce warrior and would often be in the company of Hadhrat Umar (RA). When Hadhrat Umar did not see him for a while, he asked about him. "O Ameerul Mu'mineen!" someone informed him, "He has taken to drink." Hadhrat Umar sent for his scribe and wrote the following letter addressed to the man: Peace be on you Before you do I praise Allaah besides Whom there is none worthy of worship. (Allaah is also) The Forgiver of sins, Acceptor of repentance, Severe in punishment, and All Powerful. There is none worthy of worship but Him, and all shall return to Him (after death). Thereafter, Hadhrat Umar (RA) turned to the people around him saying, "Pray to Allaah that He turns your brother's heart towards Him and that He accepts his repentance." When the man received the letter and he read it, he started repeating the words: "The Forgiver of sins, Acceptor of repentance, Severe in punishment. Allaah has warned me of His punishment and also promised to forgive me."
sources: Bukhaari in his Adab (Pg.93).

paras: Another narration adds that after repeating the words to himself several times, the man started to weep and then gave up drinking most admirably. When this news reached Hadhrat Umar (RA), the Ameerul Mu'mineen addressed the people saying, "This is what you ought to do when you see that your brother has slipped. Correct him, give him conviction (in Allaah's mercy), pray to Allaah to forgive him and never be Shaytaan's accomplices against him (by allowing him to continue and to lose hope in Allaah's mercy)."
sources: Ibn Abi Haatim.

paras: that they have Called Allaah by His 'Ismul A'zam'
sources: Abu Nu'aym, as quoted in the Tafseeroi Ibn Katheer (Vol. 4 Pg.70).

paras: Hadhrat Buraydah (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once overheard a Sahabi making du'aa saying; Jj i ill illi $ iiilll lyif ^ jjj jjj "O Allaah! I beg from You on account of the fact that I testify that You are that Allaah besides Whom there is none worthy of worship. You are The One and The Independent Who has no children, Who is not the child of anyone and Who has no equal."
To this, Rasulullaah ﷺ remarked, "You have begged from Allaah using His Ismul A'zam (The Most Majestic Name) with which anything asked for is granted and with which any du'aa is accepted."
sources: Abu Dawood, Tirmidhi, Ibn, Ibn Hibbaan and Haakim, as quoted in Targheeb wat Tarheeb (Vol. 3 Pg. 145). Nasa'ee has reported a similar narration, as quoted in Nawawi's Adhkaar (Pg.501).

paras: Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once overheard a Sahabi making du'aa saying:" ". Rasulullaah ﷺ addressed him saying, "Your du'aa has been accepted, so ask (what you want)."
sources: Tirmidhi, as quoted in Targheeb wat Tarheeb (Vol. 3 Pg.145).

paras: Hadhrat Anas bin Maalik (RA) narrates that Rasulqllaah once passed by Hadhrat Abu Ayaash Zaid bin Saamit Zuraqi 'while he was performing salaah and making the du'aa: "O Allaah! I beg from You on account of You being worthy of all praise and that there is none worthy of worship but You. O The Most Loving!

O The One Who Bestows all bounties! O the Creator of the heavens and the earth! O The Most Honourable and Generous!" To this, Rasulullaah ﷺ remarked, "You have begged from Allaah using His Ismul A'zam (Glorious Name) with which any du'aa is accepted and with which anything asked for is granted."
sources: Ahmad and Ibn Maajah.

paras: Another narration states that Hadhrat Abu Ayaash. (RA) also added the words: Ij £ ". Yet another narration states that he added, "I ask You for Jannah and seek Your protection from Jahannam."
sources: Abu Dawood, Nasa'ee, Haakim and Ibn Hibbaan.
Haakim, as quoted in Targheeb wat Tarheeb (Vol.3 Pg. 1 46).

paras: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once passed by a Bedouin who was making the following du'aa in his salaah: du'aa a person makes will definitely be accepted. The precise name is known only to the very chosen servants of Allaah and has always remained a secret to the masses.

"O The One Whom eyes cannot see, Who cannot be imagined, who is beyond description, Who is unaffected by happenings, Who cannot be overwhelmed by the vicissitudes of time, Who knows the weight of the mountains, the volume of the oceans, the number of falling raindrops, the number of leaves on the trees and everything upon which the night darkens and upon which the day brightens. No sky can hide another from Him, no surface of the earth can hide another from Him, no ocean can hide anything within its depths from Him and no mountain can conceal from Him anything within its rocks. Make the last part of my life the best, make the best of my deeds the last and make my best day be the one in which I meet You."

Rasulullaah ﷺ. appointed someone to bring the Bedouin to him as soon as he completed his salaah. Rasulullaah ﷺ had been given some gold from a certain mine and when the Bedouin came before him after he had completed his salaah, Rasulullaah ﷺ handed over the gold to him saying, "Which tribe do you belong to, dear Bedouin?" When the Bedouin informed Rasulullaah ﷺ that he belonged to the Banu Aamir bin Sa'sa'ah tribe, Rasulullaah ﷺ asked, "Do you know why I gave you this gold as a gift?" "Because of the family ties between us, 0 Rasulullaah ﷺ the Bedouin surmised. Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "While family lies have a right, I actually gave you the gold because of the beautiful manner ,n which you praise Allaah.

Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates, "I once heard Rasulullaah ﷺ make du'aa saying, 'O Allaah! I beg from You using that pure and blessed name of Yours which You love best and which you love to be taken, with which anything asked for is granted, with which you shower Your mercy when it is requested and with which You remove difficulties when asked to.' One day, Rasulullaah ﷺ said to me, 'O Aa'ishal Do you know that Allaah has informed me of the name by which any du'aa is accepted.' 'May my parents be sacrificed for you, O Rasulullaah ﷺ 1 said, 'Do teach it to me.' Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, 'It would be inappropriate for (me to teach it to) you.' I then stepped aside and sat down for awhile. Thereafter, is: I stood up, kissed his head and asked, '0 Rasulullaah fiiilr Please teach it to me.' Again Rasulullaah ﷺ said, 'It would be inappropriate for (me to teach it to) you, O Aa'isha because it would be inappropriate for you to use it to ask for anything of this world."'

Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates further. She says, "I then got up to make wudhu, after which 1 performed two Rakaahs salaah. Thereafter, I made du'aa saying: li'jfitij Ijjpiij li "O Allaah! I call to You as Allaah. I call to You as the Most Merciful. I call to You as the Most Pure and Most Kind. I call to You by all Your beautiful names that I know and those that I do not know, beseeching You to forgive me and shower Your mercy on me."

Hadhrat Salamah bin (RA) narrates. that every du'aa he heard Rasulullaah ﷺ make started with the words: Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "Even if Rasulullaah ﷺ had to make a hundred du'aas, he would always say at the beginning, in the middle and at the end: "O our Rabb! Grant us the best in this world, the best in the Aakhirah and save us from the fire of Jahannam."
sources: Ibn Maajah (Pg.698).

paras: Hadhrat Fudhaala bin Ubayd (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ was sitting (in the Masjid) one day when a man entered, performed salaah and then made du'aa saying, "O Allaah! Forgive me and have mercy on me." Addressing the man, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Dear Musalli! You have been too hasty. When sitting down after performing salaah, first praise Allaah as He deserves to be praised and then send salutations to me before making du'aa." Another Sahabi then came to perform salaah. After completing his salaah, he praised Allaah and sent salutations to Rasulullaah ijeif . Rasulullaah ﷺ then said to him, "O Musalli! Now make du'aa and it will be accepted."
sources: Abu Dawood, Tirmidhi, Nasa'ee, Ibn Hibbaan and Ibn Khuzaymah, as quoted in Targheeb wat Tarheeb (Vol. 3 Pg.147). Tabraani has reported a similar narration, as quoted in Majma'uz Zawaa'id (Vol.10 Pg.155).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "When any of you intends making du'aa, he should commence by praising Allaah as. He deserves to be praised. Thereafter, he should send salutations to Nabi ﷺ before asking his need because in this manner it is more likely that his needs will be fulfilled."
sources: Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.10 Pg.155) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Abbaas bin Mirdaas (RA) reports that during the evening Rasulullaah spent at Arafaat, he made du'aa that Allaah forgive and have mercy on his Ummah. After making du'aa for a very long time, Allaah revealed to him saying, "1 accede to your request (all will be forgiven) except for injustices people do to each other. I shall however forgive all the sins that relate to them and I." "O my Rabb!" Rasulullaah ﷺ pleaded, 'You are capable of replacing the wronged one with that which is better than the wrong done to him and then forgiving the wrong-doer." Rasulullaah ﷺ received no response to this du'aa that evening, but when he repeated the du'aa on the morning that he was at Muzdalifah, Allaah said to him, "I have now forgiven them as well." When Rasulullaah ﷺ smiled at this, the Sahabah (RA) asked, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ You are smiling at a time when you usually do not smile (at the time of Tahajjud)." Rasulullaah explained, "I am smiling at Allaah's enemy Iblees. When he came to know that Allaah has accepted the du'aa I made for my Ummah, he fell to the ground, calling for woe and destruction to himself and then poured sand on his head."
sources: Bayhaqi.

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once recited the words of Hadhrat Ibraheem (RA) when he said: "O my Rabb? Indeed these idols have misled many people. So whoever will follow me (by believing in Towheed), then he is certainly from me (from among the adherents of my religion). And whoever will disobey me, then (I pray that you give him the ability to obey me because) surely You are Most Forgiving, Most Merciful." (Surah Ibraheem, verse 36)
Rasulullaah ﷺ then recited the following words of Hadhrat Isa (RA)

"If You punish them (my followers), then verily they are Your slaves (and You are at liberty to treat them as You please), and if You forgive them, then surely You are the Mighty, the Wise (and Yam reason for doing so is filled with wisdom). "(Surah Maa'idah, verse 1 ,, Thereafter, Rasulullaah ﷺ made du'aa to Allaah saying, "O Allaah! My Ummah?

O Allaah! My Ummah! O Allaah! My Ummah!" Rasulullaah ﷺ then started to weep. Although Allaah knows all, He sent Hadhrat. Jibra'eel (RA) to ask Rasulullaah ﷺ what was making him weep. When Hadhrat Jibra'eel (RA) came to ask, Rasulullaah ﷺ informed him about what he had been saying. (After Hadhrat Jibra'eel (RA) had reported back) Allaah instructed Hadhrat Jibra'eel saying, "Go to Muhammad ﷺ and tell him, We shall soon please you regarding to your Ummah and will not disappoint you."
sources: lbn Wahab, as quoted in the Tafseer ollbn Katheer (Vol.2 Pg.540).

paras: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once made the following du'aa for his Ummah, "O Allaah! Turn their hearts to your obedience and engulf them from the back with Your mercy."

Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says that when she noticed that Rasulullaah ﷺ was in a very good mood one day, she said to him, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ Make du'aa to Allaah for me." Rasulullaah ﷺ prayed, "O Allaah! Forgive Aa'isha's every past and future sin, those that were apparent and those that were secret." This made Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) so happy that her head fell into her lap as she chuckled about it. "Does my du'aa make you happy?" Rasulullaah ﷺ asked her. She replied, "How can I not rejoice about your du'aa?" Rasulullaah ﷺ then said, "By Allaah! This is the du'aa I make for Ummah in every salaah."
Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ made du'aa saying, "O Allaah!
Include Abu Bakr in my rank on the Day of Qiyaamah."
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.4 Pg.345).

paras: Hadhrat Khabbaab (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ made du'aa saying, "O Allaah! Strengthen Islaam with the one whom You love more between Umar bin Khattaab and Abu Jahal bin Hishaam."
sources: Nasa'ee. Ahmad, Tirmidhi, Ibn Sa'd and others have reported a similar narration from Hadhrat Umar (RA).

paras: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ made du'aa saying, "O Allaah! Grant Islaam strength with Umar bin Khattaab especially."
sources: Ibn Maajah, Haakim and Bayhaqi.

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) also narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ said in his du'aa, "O Allaah! Assist Islaam through Umar."
sources: Tabraani and Ahmad, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.4 Pg.370).

paras: Hadhrat Zaid bin Aslam (RA) narrates that when Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) sent a reddish coloured camel to Rasulullaah ﷺ, Rasulullaah ﷺ prayed to Allaah saying, "O Allaah! Allow him to pass (speedily) across the bridge of Siraat."
sources: Ibn Asaakir.

paras: Another narration from Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) states that Rasulullaah ﷺ thrice said, "O Allaah! I am pleased with Uthmaan, You also be pleased with him."
sources: Abu Nu'aym.

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ made du'aa saying, "O Allaah! Forgive, Uthmaan's past and future sins, those that he committed secretly and openly, privately or in public."

Hadhrat Ali (RA) says, "I was once experiencing severe pain, so I went to Rasulullaah ﷺ. He put me where he stood, threw a portion of his shawl over me and then started performing salaah. Thereafter, he said, You are now well, O son of Abu Taalib. Your ailment has been cured. Whatever I have asked Allaah for myself, I have asked the same for you and I have been granted whatever I have asked for. I have however been informed that there shall be no prophet after me.'" Hadhrat Ali (RA) says further, "When I then got up, it seemed as if I had not had any pain at all."
sources: Tabraani, Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya and ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg.6).

paras: Hadhrat Zaid bin Yuthay, Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Wahab and Hadhrat Amr bin Dhi Murr all report that they heard Hadhrat Ali (RA) say, "It is in the name of Allaah that I ask every person to stand up who heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say something at Ghadeer Khum'9)." Thirteen Sahabah (RA) stood up and they all testified that they heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, "Am I not closer to the Mu'mineen than they are to themselves?" When the Sahabah (RA) admitted that he really was, Rasulullaah ﷺ took hold- of Hadhrat Ali (RA)'s hand saying, "This man should be the friend of anyone who claims that 1 am his friend." Rasulullaah ﷺ then made du'aa for Hadhrat Ali (RA) saying, "O Allaah! Befriend those who befriend him, be the enemy of those who are his enemies, love those who love him, despise who despise him, assist those who assist him and do not assist those who fail to assist him."
sources: Bazzaar, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.lOS).

paras: Another narration from Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) states that Rasulullaah ﷺ made du'aa for Hadhrat Ali (RA) saying, "O Allaah! Assist him and assist others through him, have mercy on him and have mercy on others though him, help him and help others though him. O Allaah! Befriend those who are his friends and be the ertemy of those who are his enemies."
sources: Tabraani, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaai '(Vol.5 Pg.32).

paras: Hadhrat Ali 5S83sS!sa reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ made du'aa for him saying, "O Allaah! Keep his tongue firm (on the truth) and guide his heart."
sources: Haakim.

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ's du'aa for Hadhrat Ali (RA) was, "O Allaah! Guide him in passing judgement."
sources: Haakim, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaai (Vol. 5 Pg.35).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) narrates that the du'aa Rasulullaah ﷺ made for Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas (RA) was, "O Allaah! Make his arrows travel straight, accept his du'aas and love him."
sources: Ibn Asaakir and Ibn Najjaar-

paras: Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) himself narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ made du'aa for him saying, "O Allaah! Accept the du'aa of Sa'd whenever he makes du'aa to You." ™ Hadhrat Zubayr bin Awwaam (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ made du'aa for him, for his children and for his progeny.
sources: Tirmidhi, Ibn Hibbaan and Haakim, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaai ' (Vol.5 Pg.70).

paras: Hadhrat Ummu Salamah (RA) who was the wife of Rasulullaah ﷺ narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once told Hadhrat Faatima (RA) to come to him with her husband and her two sons. When they arrived, Rasulullaah ﷺ threw over them a blanket that Hadhrat Ummu Salamah (RA) was sitting on, which they had received as booty from Khaybar. Rasulullaah ﷺ then prayed to Allaah saying, "O Allaah! This is the family of Muhammad. Shower Your mercy and blessings on the family of Muhammad just as You have showered them on the family of Ibraheem. Verily You are most worthy of praise, Most Majestic."
sources: Abu Ya'la. Haythami (Vol. 9 Pg.166) has commented on the chain of narrators. Tirmidhi has reported a similar narration.

paras: Hadhrat Abu Ammaar narrates that he was once sitting with Hadhrat Waathila bin Asqa when some people started to revile Hadhrat Ali (RA). When they had left, Hadhrat Waathila (RA) said to Hadhrat Abu Ammaar, "Sit down and 1 shall inform about the personality whom they had been reviling. I was once with Rasulullaah ﷺ when Ali, (his wife) Faatima, (and his two sons) Hasan and Husayn arrived. Rasulullaah ﷺ threw a blanket over them all and said, 'O Allaah! These are the members of my household. Remove all (physical and spiritual) impurity from them and cleanse them thoroughly.' 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ 1 asked, '(Make this du'aa) For me as well.' 'It is for you as well,' Rasulullaah ﷺ said. By Allaah! More than all my deeds, it is in this (du'aa) that I have the most trust (to attain my salvation)." Another narration states that he said, "It is in this that I have the most trust (to secure my salvation)."
sources: Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.167) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Ali (RA) narrates that he once went to Rasulullaah ﷺ, who had already spread out a shawl on the ground. When Rasulullaah ﷺ, Hadhrat Ali Hadhrat Faatima (RA), Hadhrat Hasan (RA) and Hadhrat Husayn SS-sSSgS were all seated on the shawl, Rasulullaah ﷺ took hold of the ends and tied it above them. Thereafter, he said, "O Allaah! You be pleased with them just as I am pleased with them."
sources: Tabraani, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.169).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once made du'aa for Hadhrat Hasan (RA) and Hadhrat Husayn (RA) saying, "O Allaah! IloveJhem,soYou love them too. Whoever loves them, loves me as well."
sources: Bazzaar, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.180).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) also reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once made du'aa for Hadhrat Hasan (RA) and Hadhrat Husayn (RA) saying, "O Allaah! I love them, so You love them too."
sources: Bazzaar.

paras: Another narration from Hadhrat Usaama states that Rasulullaah ﷺ added, "...and love those who love them." The beginning of this narration adds that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "These are my children just as they are the children of my daughter." Yet another narration from Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) like the one above states that Rasulullaah ﷺ added at then end of the du'aa, "...and (O Allaah!) detest those who detest them."
sources: Nasa'ee and Ibn Hibbaan, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Pg.105).
Ibn Abi Shaybah and Tayaalisi, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg. 1 06).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA), Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Zaid (RA) and Hadhrat Aa'isha all narrate that Rasulullaah ﷺ once made du'aa saying, "O Allaah! I love Hasan, so You love him too and love all those who love him as well."
A narration from Hadhrat Muhammad bin Seereen states that Rasulullaah ﷺ once made du'aa for Hadhrat Hasan (RA) saying, "O Allaah! Keep him safe and keep others safe through him."
sources: Bukhaari, Muslim and others, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg.406).

paras: Hadhrat Baraa (RA) says, "I once saw Rasulullaah ﷺ carrying Husayn on his shoulders saying, 'O Allaah! I love him, so You love him too.
sources: Ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal ' (Vol.5 Pg.106).

paras: Hadhrat.Abdullaah bin Abbaas narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once made du'aa saying, "O Allaah! Forgive the open and secret sins of Abbaas and his children. O Allaah! You be his successor (to tend to matters) in his family (after his death)."
sources: Bukhaari, Muslim, Tirmidhi, Ibn Maajah and Nasa'ee, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg.105).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once made du'aa saying, "O Allaah! Forgive the open and secret, the public and the private sins of Abbaas and any other sins that he or his progeny may commit until the Day of Qiyaamah."
sources: Tirmidhi and Abu Ya'la.

paras: Hadhrat Aasim narrates from his father that Rasulullaah ﷺ once said, "Abbaas is my father's brother and therefore just like my father and what is left of my forefathers. O Allaah! Forgive his sins for him, accept his good deeds, overlook his evil acts and restore righteousness to his progeny."
sources: Ibn Asaakir.

paras: Hadhrat Abu Usayd Saa'idi (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once said to Hadhrat Abbaas (RA), "You and your children should not leave the house in the morning until I come to you because there is something I need to do." They therefore waited for Rasulullaah ﷺ and it was only after midmorning that Rasulullaah ﷺ managed to arrive. When Rasulullaah ﷺ arrived, he greeted them with the words, to which they replied pi xU-jj ". "How was your morning?" Rasulullaah ﷺ asked. "We praise Allaah (for it)," they replied. Rasulullaah ﷺ then instructed them to gather together and to sit close to each other. When they managed to do so, Rasulullaah ﷺ threw his shawl over all of them and made du'aa saying, "O my Rabb! Here is my uncle, who is just like my father and here are the members of my household. Shelter them against the fire of Jahannam just as I am sheltering them with this shawl of mine." To this du'aa, the doorstep and all the walls of the house said, Ameen!

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that when he once stayed in the room of (his aunt) Hadhrat Maymoona (RA), he kept the water ready for Rasulullaah ﷺ to perform wudhu. "Who put this water here?" Rasulullaah ﷺ asked. When Hadhrat Maymoona (RA) informed Rasulullaah ﷺ that it was Hadhrat Abdullaah (RA), Rasulullaah ﷺ made du'aa for him saying, "O Allaah! Grant him deep understanding of Deen and teach him the interpretation of the Qur'aan."
sources: Ibn Najjaar, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal '(Vol. 5 Pg.231).

paras: Another narration quotes the du'aa as, "O Allaah! Teach him the Qur'aan and grant him deep understanding of the Deen." Yet another narration quotes the words as, "O Allaah! Teach him wisdom (the Sunnah) and the interpretation of the Qur'aan."
sources: Ibn Maajah, Ibn Sa'd and Tabraani.
Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal (Vol. 5 Pg.228).

paras: A narration from Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar 'ig states that Rasulullaah words were, "O Allaah! Bless him and spread the Deen through him."
sources: Ahmad and Ibn Asaakir. Tabraani and Ibn Asaakir have also reported the narration from Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Ja'far (RA) reports that Rasulullaah (icil once made du'aa saying, "O Allaah! You be Ja'far's successor in (caring for) his children."
sources: Tayaalisi, Ibn Sa'd, Ahmad and others.

paras: Another narration states that the du'aa Rasulullaah ﷺ made was, "O Allaah!
You be Ja'far's successor in (caring for) his family and bless (his son)
Abdullaah in trade." Rasulullaah ﷺ repeated this du'aa thrice.
sources: Ibn Abi Shaybah, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg.I55). Ibn Sa'd (Vol.4 Pg.39) has reported a similar narration.

paras: Hadhrat Sha'bi states that after Hadhrat Ja'far (RA) was martyred at Balqaa during the Battle of Mu'ta, Rasulullaah ﷺ made du'aa saying, "O Allaah! You be Ja'far's successor in (caring for) his family better than You would be a successor to any of Your righteous servants."
sources: Ibn Sa'd (Vol.3 Pg.46).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Maysara narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ received the news of the martyrdom of Hadhrat Zaid bin Haaritha (RA), Hadhrat Ja'far (RA) and Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Rawaaha (RA), he got up to speak about them. Starting with Hadhrat Zaid (RA), Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "O Allaah! Forgive Zaid. O Allaah! Forgive Zaid. O Allaah! Forgive Ja'far and Abdullaah bin Rawaaha."
. Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Affaan (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once made du'aa saying, "O Allaah! Forgive the family of Yaasir although you have already forgiven them."
sources: Ahmad and Ibn Sa'd.

paras: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once made du'aa saying, "O Allaah! Bless Ammaar (the son of Hadhrat Yaasir (RA) The Hadith still continues further.

Hadhrat Ummu Salamah (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once made du'aa saying, "O Allaahl Forgive Abu Salamah, elevate his rank amongst those close to You and be his successor amongst those (of his family who are) left behind. Forgive us also, O Rabb of the universe and together with expanding his grave, fill it with light as well."
sources: Ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Pg.245).

paras: Hadhrat Usaamah bin Zaid (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ used to put me on his thigh and then put Hasan bin Ali on his left thigh. Rasulullaah ﷺ would then hug us and say, "O Allaah! I am compassionate towards the two of them, You also be compassionate towards them." Another narration states that Rasulullaah ﷺ would say, "O Allaah! I love the two of them, You love them also."
sources: Ahmad, Muslim and Abu Dawood, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg.219).

paras: Hadhrat Usaamah (RA) relates, "When Rasulullaah ﷺ's illness became severe, I returned to Madinah (after camping with the Muslim army in nearby Juruf) and those with me also returned. Rasulullaah ﷺ was unable to speak when I entered (his room) and when he repeatedly placed his hand on me and lifted it, I realised that he was making du'aa for me."

Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ thrice made du'aa saying, "O Allaah! Forgive Amr bin Al Aas because whenever I request him for charity, he always brings it to me." W Hadhrat Hakeem bin Hizaam SI narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once made du'aa for him saying, "O Allaah! Bless him in trade." ^ Another narration explains that (this happened) when Rasulullaah ﷺ sent Hadhrat Hakeem (RA) to purchase a sacrificial animal for a Dinaar. After purchasing it, he sold it for two Dinaars. Thereafter, he bought another for a Dinaar and returned with (the animal and) a Dinaar to Rasulullaah ﷺ. Rasulullaah ﷺ then made du'aa that Hadhrat Hakeem (RA) be blessed (in trade) and instructed him to donate the Dinaar in Sadaqah.
sources: Abdur Razzaaq and Ibn Abi Shaybah, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg.152).

paras: Hadhrat Jareer ii says, "When I once mentioned to Rasulullaah ﷺ that I could never remain steady on horseback, he placed his hand on my chest until I could actually see its imprint on my chest. He then made du'aa saying, 'O Allaah! Make him steady and also make him one who is rightly guided and who guides others aright.' Thereafter, I never once fell off a horse."
sources: Tabraani.

paras: In another narration, Hadhrat Jareer Si! says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ once said to me, Wry do you not relieve me of Dhu Khalasa?' Dhu Khalsa was a building of the Khath'am tribe and was referred to as the Yemeni Kabah during the Period of Ignorance. 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ I submitted, 'I am a person who cannot remain steady on horseback..." The rest of the narration is like the one above.
sources: Ibn Abi Shaybah, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg.152).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Busr (RA) relates, "My father and I were sitting by the door of our house when Rasulullaah ﷺ arrived on his mule. 'O Rasulullaah my father said, "Why don't you alight to have something to eat and make du'aa for blessings?' Rasulullaah ﷺ then alighted, ate something and made du'aa saying, 'O Allaah! Have mercy on them, forgive them and bless them in their sustenance.'"' Another narration states further that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Busr said, "We then always saw a tremendous supply of sustenance coming from Allaah asas?.'."
sources: Ibn Asaakir.

paras: Hadhrat Nadhla bin Amr Ghifaari (RA) reports, "When a man from the Ghifaar tribe came to Rasulullaah ﷺ and Rasulullaah ﷺ asked him what his name was, he replied that it was Muhaan (meaning 'the disgraced one'). Rasulullaah said, You are now Mukrim ('the honoured one').' When Rasulullaah ﷺ arrived in Madinah, he also led the Janaazah salaah for Hadhrat Baraa bin Ma'roor. Rasulullaah ﷺ made du'aa for him saying, 'O Allaah! Shower Your special mercy on Baraa bin Ma'roor. Do not be unapproachable to him on the Day of Qiyaamah and enter him into Jannah, which You already have (decreed).
sources: Tabraani, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg.220).

paras: Hadhrat Ibn Abu Qataadah (RA) reports that the person for whom Rasulullaah led the Janaazah salaah when he arrived in Madinah was Hadhrat Baraa bin Ma'roor. Rasulullaah ﷺ went with the Sahabah ie and when they formed a row in front of Hadhrat Baraa (RA)'s body, Rasulullaah ﷺ made du'aa saying, "O Allaah! Forgive him, have mercy on him and be pleased with him, even though You have already done this."
sources: Ibn Sa'd Pg.620).

paras: Hadhrat Qais bin Sa'd (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once made du'aa saying, "O Allaah! Shower Your special mercy on the family of Sa'd bin Ubaadah and forgive them."
sources: Abu Dawood, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal tyo Pg.190).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Qataadah (RA) relates, "We were with Rasulullaah ﷺ on a journey when (because of exhaustion) he started to lean to one side of his animal. I then held him up with my hand until he woke up. Later when he again started to lean to one side, I again supported him until he awoke. Thereafter, he made du'aa saying, 'O Allaah! Look after Abu Qataadah as he has looked after me tonight.' He then addressed me saying, 'We have certainly given you a lot of difficulty.

Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that when Hadhrat Ummu Sulaym (RA) once requested Rasulullaah ﷺ to make du'aa for him, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "O Allaah! Grant him plenty of wealth and children and bless him in them."
sources: Abu Nu'aym and Tabraani, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg. 1 6 1 ) .

paras: Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) narrates that a man called Harmala once came to Rasulullaah ﷺ. Pointing to his tongue, he said, "O Rasulullaah (Mi! Imaan is still here while hypocrisy lurks here." He then pointed towards his heart. He then continued, "I think but a little of Allaah." Rasulullaah ﷺ made du'aa for him saying, "O Allaah! Grant him a tongue that makes Dhikr and a heart that is grateful. Allow him to love those whom I love and let all his affairs have a good ending."
sources: Abu Nu'aym, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg.142).

paras: Hadhrat Talib (RA) narrates that when he once requested Rasulullaah ﷺ to make du'aa for him, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "(I will do so) When permission is granted (by Allaah)." Rasulullaah ﷺ then waited awhile before he made du'aa saying, "O Allaah! Forgive Talib and have mercy on him. O Allaah! Forgive Talib and have mercy on him. O Allaah! Forgive Talib and have mercy on him."
sources: Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.402) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once made du'aa saying, "O Allaah! Elevate your little servant Abu Aamir above the majority of people on the Day of Qiyaamah." .Hadhrat Hassaan bin Shaddaad narrates, "When my mother arrived with a delegation to meet Rasulullaah ﷺ, she said, 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ I have come with this delegation to you so that you may make du'aa that this son of mine becomes big and good.' Rasulullaah ﷺ then performed wudhu and, passing the leftover water over my face, said, "O Allaah! Bless her in this child and make him big and good.
sources: Ibn Sa'd and Tabraani, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg.239).
Abu Nu'aym, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg. 1 67) .

paras: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates that after making the Salaam, Rasulullaah ﷺ was still facing the Qibla when he raised his head and made du'aa saying, "O Allaah! Free Salamah bin Hishaam, Ayaash bin Abu Rabee'ah, Waleed bin Waleed and all the other weak Muslim who are unable to formulate an escape route and have no way out (of Makkah)."
sources: Bazzaar. Haythami (Vol.10 Pg.152) has commented on the chain of narrators. Ibn Sa'd (Vol.4 Pg.130) has reported a similar narration.

paras: Another narration states that it was after raising his head from a Rakaah of the Fajr salaah that Rasulullaah ijcll made du'aa saying, "O Allaah! Rescue Waleed bin Waleed, Salamah bin Hishaam, Ayaash bin Abu Rabee'ah and the other oppressed Muslims in Makkah. O Allaah! Severely trample the Mudhar tribe underfoot and afflict them with drought as the people were afflicted during the The Du'aas Rasulullaah ﷺ Recited When Bidding Farewell Rasulullaah Si says: "I place your Deen in Allaah's Custody..."
sources: Ibn Sa'd (Vol.4 Pg. 130).

paras: Hadhrat Qaz'ah narrates that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) once said to him, "Come. Let me bid you farewell as Rasulullaah ﷺ bid me farewell. (Rasulullaah ﷺ said:)
Skitij ijbl "I place your Deen, your trustworthiness and the results of all your deeds in Allaah's custody"
sources: Abu Dawood (Vol.3 Pg.232).

paras: Another narration states that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) would always say to a person embarking on a journey, "Come close to me so that I may bid you farewell as Rasulullaah ﷺ bid me farewell." He would then recite the du'aa quoted above.
sources: Tirmidhi(Vol.2Pg.l82).

paras: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that a Sahabi once came to Rasulullaah saying, "O Rasulullaah iiS-?! I intend embarking on a journey, so do give me some provision (du'aas). Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "May Allaah make Taqwa your provision." When he asked for more du'aa, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "May Allaah also forgive your sins." "May my parents be sacrificed for you, O Rasulullaah the Sahabi said, "Do give me more." Rasulullaah ﷺ obliged, saying, "And may Allaah make it easy for you to acquire good wherever you may

Hadhrat Qataadah Rahaawi (RA) says, "When Rasulullaah ﷺ appointed me as leader of my people, I held his hand as he bade me farewell. Rasulullaah ﷺ said: "May Allaah make Taqwa your provision, forgive your sins and lead you towards good wherever you may be"' Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates that a man once said, "O Rasulullaah I wish to undertake a journey, so please give me some advice." Rasulullaah said, "Ensure that you always adopt Taqwa and recite ('Al iJb1)laahu Akbar') when ascending any slope." As the Sahabi was leaving, Rasulullaah ﷺ made du'aa saying: "O Allaah! Shorten the distance for him and make the journey easy for him"
sources: Tabraani and Bazzaar, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.10 Pg.131).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Umaamah (RA) reports that when Nabi ﷺ lifted the tablecloth off the ground (after eating), he would recite: "Lij .up Fiy JU "All praise that is most abundant, pure and blessed belongs to Allaah but is (of course) insufficient (to praise Him adequately). O our Rabb, we are unable to stop praising You and will never be independent of doing so either"
sources: Bukhaari, Abu Dawood and Tirmidhi.

paras: Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) reports that whenever Rasulullaah ﷺ ate or drank, he would recite: ^ Uuerj Uli-ij ij "All praise belongs to Allaah Who has given us food and drink and has made us amongst the Muslims"
sources: Tirmidhi and Abu Dawood, as quoted in Jam'ul Fawaa'id (Vol.2 Pg.264).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) reports that whenever Rasulullaah ﷺ wore a new garment, he would take the name of the garment - either a Qamees, a turban, a shawl (etc.) - and recite the following du'aa: O Allaah All praise belongs to You for giving me this (Qamees, turban, shawl, etc.) to wear. I ask You for the good of it and the good for which it was made and ask Your protection from the evil of it and the evil for which it was made"
sources: Tirmidhi and Abu Dawood, as quoted in Jam'ul Fawaa'id (Vol.2 Pg.264).

paras: Hadhrat Talha (RA) narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ sighted the new moon, he would recite: "O Allaah! Let this new moon rise over us with good fortune, Imaan, safety and Islaam. (O moon) My Rabb and yours is Allaah"
sources: Tirmidhi (Vol.2 Pg.183).

paras: A narration of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) quotes the words of the du'aa as follows: "Allaah is the Greatest! O Allaah! Let this moon rise over us with peace, security, serenity, Islaam and inspiration to do that which You love and approve of. (O moon) Our Rabb and yours is Allaah"
sources: Ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.4 Pg.326). Tabraani has reported a similar narration without the words and with the word instead of. Haythami (Vol.10 Pg.139) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Raafi bin Khadeej (RA) reports that whenever Rasulullaah ﷺ saw the new moon, he would remark, "The moon of good and virtue." He would then recite the following du'aa thrice: "O Allaah! I ask You for the good of this month and for the best of destinies and I seek Your protection from its evil"
sources: Tabraani, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.10 Pg.139).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) reports that when Rasulullaah ﷺ heard thunderclaps, he recited: "O Allaah! Let not Your wrath kill us, let not Your punishment destroy us but rather grant us safety before that"
sources: Tirmidhi, as quoted in Jam'ul Fawaa'id (Vol.2 Pg.264).

paras: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates that whenever the wind blew violently, Rasulullaah ﷺ would say: "O Allaah! I ask You for its good, the good in it and the good it has been sent for. I also seek Your protection from its evil, the evil in it and the evil (punishment) it has been sent for"
sources: Bukhaari, Muslim and Tirmidhi.

paras: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) also reports that whenever Rasulullaah ﷺ noticed a cloud forming on the horizon, he would leave what he was doing. In fact, if he was performing salaah, he would shorten it. He would then recite the du'aa: "O Allaah! I seek Your protection from its evil" If rain then fell, he would say: (lI "O Allaah! Make this a pleasant downpour"
sources: Abu Dawood, as Jam'ul Fawaa'id (Vol.2 Pg.265).

paras: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA), narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ noticed a dense cloud in the sky, he /Would forsake everything he was doing, even salaah. He would then turn to the cloud and say: "O Allaah! We seek Your protection from the evil (punishment) with which it has been sent" However, if it happened to rain, he would recite the following du'aa twice or thrice: "O Allaah! Make this a beneficial downpour"
sources: Ibn Abi Shaybah, as quoted in Kanzul Lfmmaal '(Vol. 4 Pg.290).

paras: Hadhrat Salamah bin Akwa (RA) reports that when the wind blew fiercely, Rasulullaah ﷺ would say: "O Allaah! Make it a wind that is fruitful and not one that is destructive"
sources: Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.10 Pg.135) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to make du'aa saying: ij is iulii "O Allaah! I ask you for guidance, Taqwa, chastity and independence"
sources: Muslim.

paras: Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) reports that one of the du'aas Rasulullaah often recited was: "O Allaah! Forgive my sins, my acts of ignorance, the excesses I commit in my affairs and everything else that You know better than I. O Allaah! Forgive the wrong I do in earnestness, in jest, in error and on purpose, all of which I am guilty of. O Allaah! Forgive my past sins, my future sins, those that I have done secretly, those I have committed openly and all others that You know better than I. You are the one Who promotes and relegates (people in status) and You have power over all things"
sources: Muslim and Bukhaari.

paras: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to make the following du'aa: "O Allaah! Set right the affairs of my Deen in which lies the safety of all my affairs, set right my worldly affairs in which lies my livelihood and set right the affairs of my Aakhirah to which I shall be returning. Make life a means for me to progress in every good and make death a means . for me to be relieved of every evil"'1 * Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to make the following du'aa: ti - "O Allaah! To You do I submit, in You do I believe, in You do I trust, to You do I turn and with You do I challenge (my opposition). O Allaah! Because there is none worthy of worship but You, I seek protection with Your honour against me being misguided. You are the Ever Living Who will never die while man and Jinn will surely die"'
Hadhrat Ummu Salamah (RA) narrates that the du'aa Rasulullaah ﷺ most often made was: "O the One Who turns hearts! Keep my heart steadfast on Your Deen"
sources: Muslim.

paras: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates that another of the du'aas that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to make was: Oj Co JU "O Allaah! Grant me well-being in my body and well-being in my sight and make them my beneficiaries. There is none worthy of worship but You the Most Forbearing and Most Magnanimous. Glorified is Allaah the Rabb of the Grand Throne. All praise belongs to Allaah the Rabb of the universe"' '

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that one of the du'aas Rasulullaah used to make was: "O my Rabb! Assist me and do not assist others against me. Help me and do not help others against me. Plan in my favour and do not plan against me. Guide me and make guidance easy for me and assist me against those who oppose me. O my Rabb! Make me one who is grateful to You, who remembers You, who is not wary of You, who obeys you and who turns towards You. Accept my repentance, wash away my sins, accept my du'aa, make my testimony firm, guide my heart, steer my tongue and remove ill feeling from my heart"
sources: Abu Dawood and Ibn Maajah. A narration of Tirmidhi adds the words.

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) narrates that amongst the du'aas that Rasulullaah ﷺ made was: "O Allaah! We beg You for everything that attracts Your mercy and forgiveness. We also beg You for safety from every sin, for inspiration to doeverygoodjforthe success of Jannah and safety from Jahannam."
sources: Haakim, as quoted in Nawawi's Kitaabul Adhkaar (Pg.498).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to make du'aa saying: "b fa blrj Qifc "O Allaah! Forgive the sins and wrong we do in jest, in earnestness and on purpose, all of which we are guilty of' Hadhrat Imraan bin Husayn (RA) narrates that the du'aa Rasulullaah ﷺ made most frequently was: "O Allaah! Forgive the wrongs I do in error and on purpose, those that I have done secretly and those I have committed openly, those committed in ignorance and those done intentionally"' Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to make du'aa saying: "O Allaah! Make my character beautiful just as You have made my appearance beautiful"
sources: Ahmad and Tabraani, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.10 Pg.172).

paras: Hadhrat Ummu Salamah (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to say: "O my Rabb! Forgive me, have mercy on me and guide me to the most upright path"
sources: Ahmad, Tabraani and Bazzaar, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.10 Pg.172).

paras: Hadhrat Anas bin Maalik (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to make du'aa saying: "O Defender of Islaam and the Muslims! Keep me steadfast on Islaam until the day I meet You"
sources: Tabraani, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.10 Pg.176).

paras: Hadhrat Busr bin Abu Artaat Qurashi (RA) reports that he heard Rasulullaah make the following du'aa: oi oiji jy j "O Allaah! Conclude all our affairs in a most beautiful manner and save us from disgrace in this world as well as the punishment of the Aakhirah"
sources: Ahmad.

paras: Another narration adds that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Whoever recites this du'aa will die before being put through tribulations."
sources: Tabraani -reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.10 Pg.187).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Sirma (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to say: "O Allaah! I ask You to grant independence to me and to all those associated with me"
sources: Ahmad and Tabraani, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.10 Pg.178).

paras: Hadhrat Thowbaan (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to make du'aa saying: "O Allaah! I ask You for all that is lawful, for the resolve to stay away from evil, for the love of the poor and to accept my repentance. When You intend putting Your servants through tribulation, I ask You to take me away without undergoing any of it"
sources: Bazzaar, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.10 Pg.181).

paras: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates that one of the du'aas Rasulullaah ﷺ used to make was: "O Allaah! Allocate the greatest quantity of the sustenance you give me to my old age and to the period just before my death"
sources: Tabraani, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.10 Pg.182).

paras: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ loved making comprehensive du'aas and would make them rather than any other."
sources: Ibn Abi Shaybah, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.1 Pg.291).

paras: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) also reports that she was busy performing salaah when (her father) Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) came to tell Rasulullaah ﷺ something that she was unable to hear. "O Aa'isha!" Rasulullaah ﷺ said to her, "Ensure that you make comprehensive du'aas. When she had completed her salaah, Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) asked Rasulullaah ﷺ about this and he advised her to make the following du'aa: JUst ^ pi U "O Allaah! I ask You for all good that is immediate and that is still to come, whether I am aware of it or not. I seek Your protection from all evil that is immediate and that is still to come, whether I am aware of it or not. I ask You for Jannah and every word and deed that will take me closer to it. I also seek Your protection from Jahannam and every word and deed that will take me closer to it. I ask You for every good that Your servant and Rasul Muhammad ﷺ asked You for and I seek Your protection from everything that Your servant and Rasul Muhammad sought Your protection from. I also beseech You to make the outcome be good of everything that You have decreed for me"
sources: Haakim, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.1 Pg.306). Ahmad and Ibn Maajah have reported a similar narration, as quoted in the Adhkaar of Nawawi.

paras: In another narration, Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "I was busy performing salaah when Nabi ﷺ entered the room. He needed something and because I was delaying him, he said, 'O Aa'isha! You ought to make du'aa that is concise and comprehensive.' When I completed, I asked, 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ What du'aa is concise and comprehensive?'" Rasulullaah ﷺ then taught her the du'aa quoted above.
sources: Bukhaari in his Adab (Pg.506).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Umaamah (RA) says that because Rasulullaah ﷺ made so many du'aas, they were unable to remember them. They therefore said to him one day, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ You make so many du'aas, that we are unable to remember them." Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Should I not teach you a du'aa that incorporates all of them?" Rasulullaah ﷺ then told them to recite: "We ask You for every good that Your Nabi ﷺ asked You for and we seek Your protection from everything that Your Nabi Muhammad ﷺ sought Your protection from. It is only from You that help can be sought and only You can conclude all matters because there is no power or might but from Allaah"
sources: Tirmidhi (Vol.2 Pg.190). Bukhaari has reported a similar narration in his Adab (Pg.99).

paras: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to make du'aa saying: "O Allaahl 1 seek Your protection from helplessness, laziness, cowardice, extreme old age and miserliness. I also seek Your protection from punishment in the grave and from the tribulations of life and death" Another narration adds the words: "...(and I seek Your protection from) the burden of debts and from the tyranny of men"
sources: Bukhaari and Muslim.

paras: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to include the following words in his du'aa: "O Allaah! I seek Your protection from the evil of what 1 do and from the evil of what I do not do"
sources: Muslim:

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) narrates that amongst the du'aas that Rasulullaah ﷺ made was: "O Allaah! I seek Your protection from losing Your bounties, from a reverse in well-being, from sudden calamities and from all forms of Your wrath" Hadhrat Zaid bin Arqam (RA) once said to the people, "I am telling you only what Rasulullaah ﷺ used to tell us." (He then proceeded to teach them the following du'aa:)

"O Allaah! I seek Your protection from helplessness, laziness, cowardice, miserliness and from punishment in the grave. O Allaah! Grant Taqwa to my Nafs and purify it because You are the best of those who purify il. You are its Protector and Master. O Allaah! I seek Your protection from knowledge that does not benefit, from a heart that does not fear (displeasing You), from a Nafs that is never satiated and from du'aas that are not accepted"

Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ used the following words when making du'aa: "O Allaah! I seek Your protection from the tribulation of Jahannam, from its punishment and from the evils of both wealth and poverty"
sources: Tirmidhi, Abu Dawood, Ibn Maajah and Nasa'ee.

paras: Hadhrat Qutba bin Maalik (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to make the following du'aa: "O Allaah! 1 seek Your protection from character, actions and desires that are evil"
sources: Tirmidhi.

paras: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to make du'aa saying: "O Allaah! I seek Your protection from leprosy, insanity and all debilitating diseases"
sources: Abu Dawood and Nasa'ee.

paras: Hadhrat Abu Yasar (RA) who was also a Sahabi reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to make du'aa saying: "O Allaah! 1 seek Your protection from being crushed, from falling, from drowning, from being burnt and from extreme old age. I also beseech You to protect me from being driven insane by Shaytaan at the time of death, from dying in Your path while fleeing from the battlefield and from dying from the bite of a poisonous creature"
sources: Abu Dawood and Nasa'ee.

paras: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to make the following du'aa: "O Allaah! I seek Your protection from starvation because it is the worst of companions and I seek Your protection from treachery because it is the worst of confidantes"
sources: Abu Dawood and Nasa'ee, as quoted in Kitaabul Adhkaar (Pg.499).

paras: Another narration states that Rasulullaah ﷺ used say in his du'aas: "O Allaah! I seek Your protection from disputes, hypocrisy and bad character"
sources: Abu Dawood and Nasa'ee, as quoted in Tayseerul Wusool (Vol.2 Pg.83).

paras: Hadhrat Anas (RA) -reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to recite the following du'aa: ,-4-j Uj O Allaah! 1 seek Your protection from helplessness, laziness, hard-heartedness, negligence, poverty, disgrace and destitution. I seek Your protection from sinfulness, disputes, hypocrisy, boastfulness and ostentation. I also seek Your protection from being deaf, dumb, insane and from contracting leprosy or any other debilitating diseases"' '

Hadhrat Uqba bin Aamir (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to make the following du'aa: "O Allaah! I seek Your protection from a terrible day, a terrible night, a terrible moment, a terrible companion and from a terrible neighbour to my permanent residence" , Hadhrat Umar (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to seek Allaah's protection from five factors with the following words: "O Allaah! I seek Your protection from miserliness, cowardice, corruption of the heart, punishment in the grave and extreme old age"
sources: Tabraani in his Sagheer, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.10 Pg.143).
Ahmad, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abu Dawood, Nasa'ee and others.

paras: Hadhrat Umar (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ used the following words to secure Allaah's protection for (his grandsons) Hadhrat Hasan (RA) and Hadhrat Husayn "In the complete and perfect attributes of Allaah do I ask: ot ^ ^ 4?' rotection for the two of you from every Shaytaan and harmful creature and from every evil eye"
sources: Abu Nu'aym in, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.1 Pg.212).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Tayyaah narrates that he once asked Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Khambash Taymi - who was an old man by then - "Did you meet Rasulullaah ﷺ When the Sahabi confirmed that he did, Hadhrat Abu Tayyaah asked, "What did Rasulullaah ﷺ do the night the Jinn connived against him?" Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan (RA) explained, "That night many Jinn came down from their mountains and valleys to (attack) Rasulullaah ﷺ. Amongst them was a particular Shaytaan who carried a flame in his hand with the intention of burning the blessed face of Rasulullaah ﷺ. However, Hadhrat Jibra'eel came down to Rasulullaah ﷺ saying, 'O Muhammad ﷺ Say something!' 'What shall I say?' Rasulullaah ﷺ asked. Hadhrat Jibra'eel (RA) then told Rasulullaah ﷺ to recite the following words: tU-JI Jji) Iji) iL 'In the complete and perfect attributes of Allaah do I ask protection from the evil of everything He has created and dispersed and from the evil of everything descending from the sky and going up into it. I also seek protection from the evil of the trials of the day and night and from every occurrence except those that bring good. O The Most Merciful (it is to You that I plead)'
(After Rasulullaah ﷺ recited the du'aa) The flame they carried was then extinguished and Allaah defeated them."
sources: Ahmad and Abu Ya'la, as quoted in Targheeb wat Tarheeb (Vol.3 Pg. 1 1 7) with commentary on the chain of narrators. Nasa'ee and Ibn Abi Shaybah have reported similar narrations, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.1 Pg.212).

paras: Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b (RA) reports that he was once with Rasulullaah ﷺ when a Bedouin came and said, "O Nabi of Allaah ! I have a brother who is suffering." "What is it that ails him?" Rasulullaah ﷺ asked. When the man explained that his brother was affected by the Jinn, Rasulullaah ﷺ told him to bring his brother to him. (When the man came) Rasulullaah ﷺ seated the man in front of him and recited the following to secure protection for him (against the Jinn): • Surah Faatiha • the first four verses of Surah Baqarah • the verse: yi Jllj ^ ill (Surah Baqarah, verse 1 63) • Aayatul Kursi • Three verses at the end of Surah Baqarah • The verse: ■i Art (Surah Aal Imraan, verse 18) • The verse Ji M oj" ljj iill 'y'is'i jiill Jj "Ji ajJ jlillj (Surah A'raaf, verse 54) • The concluding verses of Surah Mu'mineen, starting from • The verse: il (Surah Jinn, verse 3) • Ten verses from the beginning of Surah Saaffaat • Three verses at the end of Surah Hashar • Surah Ikhlaas • Surah Falaq and Surah Naas (After Rasulullaah ﷺ recited these before him) The man then stood up as if he had never had any ailment whatsoever.
sources: Tabraani, as quoted in Targheeb wat Tarheeb (Vol.3 Pg. 1 1 6). Haythami (Vol.10 Pg.127) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Abu Umaamah (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Khaalid bin Waleed (RA) once told Rasulullaah (iei!? about the frightening dreams that he saw, which prevented him from performing salaah at night. "O Khaalid bin Waleed Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Should I not teach you some words that if you say thrice, Allaah will dispel these dreams from you?" "May my parents be sacrificed for you, O Rasulullaah ﷺ Hadhrat Khaalid (RA) exclaimed, "Do inform rhe because it was precisely for this reason that I told you about this." Rasulullaah ﷺ then told him to recite the following du'aa: "I seek protection in the complete and perfect attributes of Allaah from His wrath, His punishment and from the evil of His servants. I also seek His protection from the whispering of the Shayaateen and from them approaching me"

Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) relates further that it was not even a few nights later that Hadhrat Khaalid (RA) came back to Rasulullaah ﷺ saying, "May my parents be sacrificed for you, O Rasulullaah ﷺ I swear by the Being Who has sent you with the truth that when I thrice completed the words you taught me, Allaah dispelled the condition I was suffering from. I now do not even fear entering a lion's den at night."
sources: Nasa'ee, Abu Dawood, Haakim and Tirmidhi.

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr (RA) mentioned that the above du'aa should be recited whenever a dream scares a person. He therefore used to teach the du'aa to those children of his who were of an understanding age. As for those who had not yet reached the age of understanding, he would write the du'aa down on a piece of paper and tie it around their necks.
sources: Nasa'ee. Maalik has reported a similar narration in his Mu'atta.

paras: Another narration states that Hadhrat Khaalid bin Waleed (RA) often woke up frightened from his sleep. When he mentioned this to Rasulullaah ﷺ, Rasulullaah ﷺ advised him thafas soon as he awoke, he should recite (Bismillaah), followed by the du'aa Quoted above.
sources: Ahmad, as quoted in Targheeb wat Tarheeb (Vol.3 Pg. 116).

paras: Another narration states that when Hadhrat Waleed bin Waleed (RA) told Rasulullaah ﷺ that he often felt fearful, Rasulullaah ﷺ advised him to recite the above du'aa when he retired to bed.
sources: Ahmad, Nasa'ee, Ibn Jareer, Ibn Hibbaan and others, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.1 Pg.298). Haakim has reported a similar narration, as quoted in Tuhfatudh Dhaakireen (Pg.194).

paras: Hadhrat Ali (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ instructed me to recite the following du'aa whenever I faced any difficulty: tA iiji t "There is none worthy of worship but Allaah the Most Forbearing and Most Magnanimous. Glorified and Blessed is Allaah the Rabb of the Glorious throne. All praise belongs to Allaah the Rabb of the universe A narration of the type has already been quoted in the chapter discussing how Adhkaar were taught.
Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that whenever Rasulullaah ﷺ was faced with any difficulty, he used to recite: "O The Ever Living and Controller, it is by Your mercy that I seek assistance"
sources: Ibn Najjaar, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal Pg.299).

paras: Hadhrat Asmaa bint Umays (RA) narrates that whenever Rasulullaah ﷺ was perturbed about something or when he was faced with some difficulty, he would recite: "Allaah! Allaah is my Rabb and I shall not ascribe any as partner to Him"
sources: Ibn Jareer.

paras: In another narration, Hadhrat Asmaa (RA) says that Rasulullaah ﷺ taught her to the above du'aa when in difficulty.
sources: Ibn Jareer and Ibn Abi Shaybah, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol. 1 Pg.300) .

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports that they were inside a room when Rasulullaah ﷺ held on to the door-frame and told them, "O family of Abdul Muttalib! When you experience any difficulties or hardships, say: "Allaah! Allaah is our Rabb and we shall not ascribe any as partner to Him"
sources: Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.10 Pg.137) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Another narration quotes the same narration with the words: "Allaah! Allaah has no partner"
sources: Ibn Jareer, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol. 1 Pg.300).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to recite the following du'aa during times of difficulty: ij ill Ij iill ilj ijbl 2)J T "There is none worthy of worship but Allaah the Most Honoured and The Most Forbearing. There is none worthy of worship but Allaah the Rabb of the Glorious throne. There is none worthy of worship but Allaah the Rabb of the heavens, the Rabb of the earth and the Rabb of the Majestic Throne"
sources: Bukhaari and Muslim, as quoted in Tuhfatudh Dhaakireen (Pg.193).

paras: Hadhrat Thowbaan (RA) reports that whenever something alarmed Rasulullaah ﷺ, he would say: "Allaah! Allaah is my Rabb and I shall not ascribe any as partner to Him"
sources: Ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol. 1 Pg.300) .

paras: Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) once mentioned that whether with sincerity or not, when a person recites the following du'aa seven times, Allaah will alleviate all his worries: "Allaah is enough for me (to alleviate all my worries). There is none worthy of worship but He. In Him do I pin my trust and He is the Rabb of the Glorious Throne" It is reported then whenever Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) recited the following du'aa, it was accepted, whether he recited it for any anxiety or worry or for fear of any ruler: "I ask You on the strength of my belief that there is none worthy of worship but You, the Rabb of the seven heavens and Rabb of the Glorious Throne. I ask You on the strength of my belief that there is none worthy of worship but You, the Rabb of the seven heavens and Rabb of the Honoured Throne. I ask You on the strength of my belief that there is none worthy of worship but You, the Rabb of the seven heavens and seven earths and everything in them. Verily You have power over all things" It is after saying this that a person should ask Allaah for what he needs.
sources: Haakim, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.1 Pg.300).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Raafi narrates that when Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Ja'far (RA) (under duress) married his daughter to (the notorious governor) Hajjaaj bin Yusuf, he advised her to recite the following du'aa whenever Hajjaaj came to her: C/j Jb Co ?! 2JJ"5"
"There is none worthy of worship but Allaah The Most Forbearing and The Most Magnanimous. Pure is Allaah The Rabb of the Majestic Throne. All praise belongs to Allaah the Rabb of the universe"
He believed that it was this du'aa that Rasulullaah ﷺ always recited whenever he was worried about something. As a result (of her reciting this du'aa) Hajjaaj was unable to get close to her.
sources: Ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.1 Pg.300).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) said, "When you appear before a fearsome ruler and you fear that he may tyrannise you, then recite the following du'aa three times: Jul iw Jri 'ot li «■/" Lftfj o?

'Allaah is the Greatest! Allaah is the Greatest! Allaah is Mightier than all of the creation and Mightier than anything I fear and am apprehensive about. I seek the protection of that Allaah besides whom there is none worthy of worship, the One Who holds the seven skies from falling to the earth without His permission. I seek Your protection from this servant of Yours, from his army, his followers and all his partisans from amongst Jinn and mankind. O Allaah! Be my Protector against their evil. Exalted are Your praises, mighty is Your protection, blessed is Your name and there is none worthy of worship but You.
sources: Ibn Abi Shaybah, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.1 Pg.300). Tabraani has reported a similar narration from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.10 Pg.137). Bukhaari has also reported a similar narration in his Adab (Pg.104).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said that if a person has a ruler whom he fears for his arrogance and oppression, he should recite: "O Allaah Rabb of the seven heavens and Rabb of the Glorious Throne. Be my Protector from this servant of Yours, from his armies and all his partisans from amongst Jinn and mankind. O Allaah! You protect me from their oppression and tyranny. Mighty is Your protection, exalted are Your praises and there is none worthy of worship but You' Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) added that when one recites this du'aa, the tyrant will be unable to do anything unpleasant to him.
sources: Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Jareer, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.1 Pg.300). Bukhaari has briefly reported a similar narration in his Adab (Pg.104).

paras: In another narration, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "If you fear a tyrannical ruler, say..." The words of the du'aa are as quoted above, but with the words: " Be my Protector against ..." After this, the name of the tyrant is to be mentioned. Thereafter, the du'aa continues as follows: "...and from the evil of the Jinn, of mankind and all their followers. I seek Your protection against any of them harming me. Mighty is Your protection, exalted are Your praises and there is none worthy of worship but You"
sources: Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.10 Pg.137) has commented on the chain of narrators.
